On the eve of Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the decade-long development process of the foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentions former Apple CEO Tim Cook's involvement in the project and reveals the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman stated that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after returning from a business trip to China, Cook was "unusually excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable device.

Cook generally "does not participate in the conception of new products," so his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone has added weight to the project:

As for the pricing of this foldable iPhone (internally referred to by Apple as the iPhone Ultra), the company's initial target was an entry-level price of US$1,999. However, recent increases in component costs have raised the target to US$2,199.

According to one of the insiders, Apple recently discussed raising the price of the foldable product to US$2,199, noting that several options had been considered in recent weeks, and memory shortages have significantly pushed up Apple's cost targets. Higher storage capacity versions may be priced close to US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on-site at the Steve Jobs Theater to provide in-depth coverage.
